context.body: The bounded canonical source is Judges 21:1–25; its local speaker, audience, sequence, and literary form remain controlling evidence.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: An oath against Benjamin creates grief over a missing tribe, and Israel answers through killing at Jabesh Gilead and abducting women at Shiloh.
observations.label: Israel tries to preserve Benjamin through further violence: action

observations.body: the book ends by saying there was no king and everyone did what was right in his own eyes.
observations.label: Israel tries to preserve Benjamin through further violence: response

observations.body: israel · tries · preserve · benjamin · through · further · violence
observations.label: Words in Judges 21:1–25

payload.posture: Read Judges 21:1–25 as tribes in the land evidence before carrying it into another source.
payload.tension: Concern for tribal survival produces new victims, and the closing diagnosis does not by itself claim that any king would solve the problem.
payload.title: Israel tries to preserve Benjamin through further violence
